perspective:
**Brandon Talayumptewa’s accessible information:**

- Brandon knows he is an insurance agent. He meets Benjamin Erickson, an entrepreneur, professionally because Benjamin seeks business insurance advice. Brandon is aware Benjamin has limited formal education and is concerned about explaining complex insurance details clearly.
- In their first meeting, Brandon hears Benjamin request comprehensive coverage and admit some insurance terms are new. Brandon explains liability insurance as a safety net and gives the slip-and-fall example; he explains asset protection as covering inventory/equipment and uses a guard analogy. Benjamin says this simplifies things and thanks him.
- In a second meeting, Brandon has revised his view of Benjamin’s ability to understand details and feels more confident. He discusses business interruption insurance and property insurance. He hears Benjamin say he has been reading up, that interruption coverage sounds crucial in unpredictable times, and that comprehensive coverage is reassuring.
- At a casual lunch, Brandon feels insecure about how Benjamin perceives his cautious/detail-oriented nature. He tells Benjamin he worries about getting too detailed and wants to keep discussions interesting. Benjamin says he appreciates the thoroughness but also enjoys lighter moments. Brandon tells a joke about an entrepreneur insuring his taste buds; Benjamin responds with interest. Brandon compares assessing unusual risks to Benjamin’s business risks, and Benjamin agrees.
- Later, Brandon feels pleased by Benjamin’s positive response to his anecdotes and wants to offer more value beyond insurance. He asks whether Benjamin has considered strategic investments to lower premiums; Benjamin has not but likes the idea. Brandon suggests upgrading security systems to protect assets and reduce insurance costs. Benjamin calls it a win-win and agrees to explore it.
- Encouraged by their rapport and mutual benefit, Brandon proposes a joint venture: co-developing a platform integrating risk management with financial planning for entrepreneurs. Benjamin agrees, calls it groundbreaking, and suggests drafting initial plans.
- Brandon experiences their relationship as evolving from insurance advice toward a stronger professional collaboration and common ground.

**Not accessible to Brandon:** Benjamin’s private thoughts, unspoken motives, personality-label information, exact education level beyond “limited formal education,” and any narrator-only information not expressed or observed in their interactions.
